overview: Cohort of index discharges built from existing hospital pharmacy dispensing records linked to regional admission and emergency department data, following adults aged 70 and over for 90 days after discharge.
population: Adults aged 70 and over discharged alive from the medical wards between 1 October 2024 and 30 September 2026, first eligible discharge per patient; excluded are discharges to palliative care, stays under 24 hours and residence outside the regional catchment.
exposure: Anticholinergic burden score at discharge from all dispensed regular medicines with the hospital's drug-weighting score (0 to 3 points per drug): exposed 3 or more, comparator 0 to 2; secondary categories 0, 1 to 2, 3 to 4 and 5 or more.
procedures: After the information governance decision, the informatics analyst extracts discharge and dispensing records; the data custodian links them to regional admission and emergency records by health number and returns a de-identified analysis file with shifted dates. Frailty comes from discharge diagnoses with a diagnosis-based frailty score that excludes medicine-related codes; indication groups (urinary incontinence, depression, psychosis, allergy, sleep problems) come from diagnoses and medicines. Follow-up runs from discharge to the first injurious fall, death or day 90; days spent in hospital after a readmission are excluded from time at risk.

outcomes.name: Injurious fall within 90 days
outcomes.measure: First emergency visit or admission at any of the three regional hospitals coded for a fall with injury
outcomes.why: Falls with injury are what patients and the consultants care about and what deprescribing review would aim to prevent.

outcomes.name: Hip fracture within 90 days
outcomes.measure: Admission with a hip fracture code
outcomes.why: The most serious and most reliably coded injury.

outcomes.name: Any fall-related hospital contact
outcomes.measure: Emergency visit or admission coded for a fall with or without injury
outcomes.why: Captures falls that reach hospital without a coded injury.

outcomes.name: Completeness of burden scoring
outcomes.measure: Proportion of index discharges with every regular medicine mapped to the burden score

feasibility: About 40 analyst hours for extraction and linkage preparation, within the stated cap; no new data collection; analysis within six months of data access approval.
biasMitigation: Frailty measured from discharge diagnoses with medicine-related codes removed, adjusted for in all models
New-user sensitivity analysis limited to medicines started during the admission
Active-comparator sensitivity analysis for bladder antimuscarinics versus beta-3 agonists
Negative control outcome (admission for cellulitis) to detect residual confounding
30-day exposure window as a sensitivity analysis to limit misclassification

biasFlags.label: Confounding by frailty
biasFlags.note: The central threat and the reason the leads conflict.

biasFlags.label: Confounding by indication
biasFlags.note: Handled by indication adjustment and the active-comparator analysis.

biasFlags.label: Exposure misclassification
biasFlags.note: Grows after 30 days because refills are not visible.

biasFlags.label: Outcome ascertainment outside the region
biasFlags.note: Falls treated outside the three hospitals are missed; the residence filter limits this.

flags: Twelve covariates fixed before data access, about 30 events per variable
Three named sensitivity analyses and no others
parsimony.simplestPath: One exposure contrast, one primary outcome, one pre-specified covariate set, one cause-specific Cox model.

theoreticalFramework: Target trial emulation as a planning device to define eligibility, exposure and time zero at discharge; no other framework.
summary: Cohort from existing linked data with one primary outcome, two secondary outcomes, a process check and three pre-specified sensitivity analyses.
